title: Code of
Conduct
cover.lede: Not an imposition — a shared framework so we can work together smoothly, professionally and with respect for one another.

pages.title: How we work
pages.intro: Joining the Software Development Club as a core member means joining a team that runs real events, ships real projects and represents the club to the whole university. These are the habits that make that possible.

clauses.title: Communication
points: Our official channel is the club's WhatsApp groups. Keep work discussions there so everyone stays informed.
Prompt responses are expected, especially to your Lead and to time-sensitive messages.
Share progress, questions and blockers early — silence is the one update nobody can act on.

clauses.title: Attendance and punctuality
points: Regular attendance at meetings, gatherings, discussions and club events is expected.
Be on time. If you cannot make it, tell your Lead in advance.
A deadline you accept is a commitment to the rest of the team.

clauses.title: Ownership and accountability
points: Take ownership of the tasks you are given and see them through.
If something gets difficult, raise it with your Lead early rather than staying silent.
Deliver what you commit to, reliably.

clauses.title: Respect and collaboration
points: Acknowledge and appreciate everyone's contributions, big or small.
Treat every member with courtesy, regardless of role, year or experience.
Help other teams when they need it — every event is a club effort.

clauses.title: Conduct in groups
points: Keep official groups professional, especially in front of juniors, participants and guests.
Keep them on topic: no spam, no arguments, no forwards unrelated to club work.
Our behaviour sets the tone for the whole club.

clauses.title: Resolving disagreements
points: Address disagreements calmly and respectfully.
Never escalate a conflict in a public group. Resolve it privately, or bring it to your Lead.

clauses.title: Solutions over blame
points: When something goes wrong, focus on fixing it rather than on who caused it.
Own your mistakes, learn from them and move forward together.

clauses.title: Keep growing
points: Keep up a regular practice of DSA and coding problems to sharpen your technical skills while you are part of the club.
Attend the club's sessions, share what you learn and help others learn too.

pages.title: Integrity and trust
pages.intro: The club runs on trust — between members, with our partners and with the university. These points protect it.

clauses.title: Confidentiality
points: Internal plans, sponsor and partner discussions, budgets, credentials and internal chats stay inside the club.
Do not share screenshots of internal groups outside the club.

clauses.title: Club resources and accounts
points: Get your Lead's approval before using club resources, funds, equipment or accounts.
Keep club files on club accounts and drives. Never share passwords or access.

clauses.title: Original work and credit
points: Plagiarism, or passing off someone else's work as your own, is not acceptable.
Credit your collaborators, and respect the licences of fonts, images and code you use.

clauses.title: Using AI tools
points: AI tools are welcome in club work, but you own the result: check it before it goes out.
Never paste confidential information or credentials into an AI tool.
Do not present AI output as your own where originality is judged, such as competitions and hackathons.

clauses.title: Representing the club
points: Online and at events, you represent the Software Development Club.
Do not post or speak on the club's behalf without approval, and keep disputes out of public view.

clauses.title: Respect and inclusion
points: Harassment, discrimination, bullying or abusive language toward anyone, in person or online, is never acceptable.
Everyone deserves to feel safe and welcome in the club.

pages.title: Raising issues
pages.intro: Most problems are solved with a conversation. Here is who to talk to, and what happens when the code is not followed.

steps.what: Your first point of contact for your work, your concerns and your ideas. You always have the right to suggest ideas to them.
If your concern is not heard, or your Lead cannot be reached, take the matter to either of them directly.

ladder.label: If the code is not followed

steps.what: For a first instance, such as a missed deadline, unexplained absence or unprofessional message.
If the issue continues or repeats after a verbal warning. It is recorded.
If the issue continues after a written warning. Issued by letter.

severe.label: Immediate termination
severe.intro: Some conduct skips the warnings entirely:
points: Leaking internal club information.
Harassment, discrimination or serious disrespect toward anyone.
Conduct that brings the club into disrepute.

appeal.label: Right to appeal
appeal.text: Any disciplinary decision can be appealed in writing to the Vice President within seven days. Every appeal is considered and answered.

pages.title: Our teams
pages.intro: You will report to your team's Lead and Co-Lead. Here is what each team does.

teams.name: Technical
teams.role: The backbone of the club's technical work.
teams.duties: Builds and maintains the club's applications, website and tools; sets up technical infrastructure for events, workshops and hackathons; leads technical sessions and supports other teams.

teams.name: Event Management
teams.role: Plans and runs every club event, from idea to wrap-up.
teams.duties: Prepares event plans, schedules and logistics; coordinates requirements across teams; runs the event on the day, handles issues on the spot and follows up afterwards.

teams.name: Design
teams.role: Keeps the club's visual identity consistent and professional.
teams.duties: Creates posters, banners, social creatives and certificates in the club's design system; designs event visuals and decor; supplies design assets to other teams.

teams.name: Public Relations and Outreach
teams.role: Builds the club's public image and relationships beyond the club.
teams.duties: Secures sponsorships and partnerships; invites speakers and industry experts; reaches out to other clubs, colleges, communities and alumni; drives promotion and attendance.

teams.name: Social Media and Content
teams.duties: Manages posts and stories on Instagram and LinkedIn; covers events in photos; writes announcements, captions, reports and newsletters; keeps the content calendar.

teams.name: Videography and Editing
teams.role: Tells the club's story on video.
teams.duties: Shoots event coverage, interviews and behind-the-scenes footage; edits reels, aftermovies and promos; keeps the footage archive; delivers edits to Social Media and Content on time.

pages.closing: This code exists so that every member can do their best work in a club they are proud of. Read it, live by it, and hold one another to it — kindly.
